title: Dual-Nerve Architecture — USB Hardwire + WiFi Wireless
principle: Two nerves connect grapheneGate to northGate: USB 3.1 (CPU-direct, 5Gbps, 0 latency) and WiFi (1134 Mbps, 73ms). USB = spinal cord. WiFi = peripheral nervous system.

usb_nerve.path: Pixel dwc3-gadget → USB Root Hub 3.0 → AMD xHCI DEV_15B7 → PCIe Root Port DEV_14DD → PCIe Root Complex PNP0A08 → CPU silicon
usb_nerve.note: Not chipset, not ASMedia — straight into Zen 5 silicon. Shortest possible path from phone to CPU.

wifi_nerve.path: Pixel wlan0 → Aperture Science 5GHz → Router (.1) → MikroTik (.2) → northGate eth0

status.ollama: DOWN — needs restart after BIOS reboot

usb_hid_gadget.description: Pixel learns USB HID gadget mode → becomes a keyboard → types into BIOS during boot
usb_hid_gadget.how: dwc3-gadget → configfs → g_hid → /dev/hidg0 → send keystrokes to host
usb_hid_gadget.enables: Fully automated BIOS surgery. No human fingers needed. The phone IS the hands.
usb_hid_gadget.prerequisite: Linux kernel on Pixel with CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_HID (GrapheneOS may not have it)

bios_surgery.method: Manual for now: power off → DEL → navigate BIOS → save → reboot
bios_surgery.future: Pixel sends DEL keystroke at POST → navigates BIOS menus → saves → reboots

body_analogy.usb: Spinal cord — hardwired, fastest, direct to brain
body_analogy.wifi: Peripheral nerves — wireless, everywhere, slight delay
body_analogy.pixel: The hand — it can think about what to type (not just dumb keystrokes)
body_analogy.northgate: The heart — most powerful compute, needs the probe for surgery
